correctness.rationale: The theorem is mathematically correct, with two sign-wording errors in its written proof. In line 23 weak stability requires nondecreasing, not nonincreasing, energy under a flip. In line 27 after the even-n neutral leaf flip it is the hub parallel to the resulting leaf majority that flips downhill, not the antiparallel hub. Independently, H=J(st+(s+t)L) for hub spins s,t and leaf sum L; for opposite hubs the two costs are 2J(1-sL), 2J(1+sL). This gives the weak census, its central-binomial asymptotics, and the excited energy -J. Aligned hubs require every leaf opposite for weak stability; the two resulting states are strict at energy J(1-2n), including n=2. For even n a neutral leaf flip from L=0 gives |L|=2, and the correct parallel hub costs -2J. For odd n>=3, the hub parallel to L at |L|=1 is neutral; after flipping it there is an aligned leaf that can flip for -4J. No nonground state can belong to a closed class: a nonweak state has a downhill exit and an excited weak state has the verified neutral/downhill path. Finite-state time-homogeneous rates positive on those edges imply almost-sure absorption. Submitted checker was inspected, not executed; the result follows by direct algebra and the allowed-move graph.

evidence: With (a,b)=(2,n), the earlier formula gives Q(1,j)=n+1 independent of j and Q=2n in the two optimal cuts. Since |E|=2n+1 this gives the claimed two energy levels and gap.
At i=1 the earlier inequalities give neutral leaf flips and permit a core-one flip for j>=(n+1)/2 or a core-zero flip for j<=(n-1)/2, neutral only at equality.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For even n, j=n/2 is one neutral leaf move from a strict core threshold. For odd n, j=(n±1)/2 is already at equality for a neutral core flip, after which there is a misaligned leaf and hence a downhill leaf flip. This directly supplies the entire short-escape refinement from the prior local rules. The tripartite Ising record is only a related mechanism in a different model, not the basis for this implication.

originality.rationale: The census is an exact specialization of an existing fixed-point theorem on complete split graphs. The absorption claim is a specialization of an existing maximum-cut attractor theorem for the same allowed-move graph. The energy values and the at-most-two-flip escape follow directly from the exact cut formula and update inequalities in the latter proof. Arbitrary positive rates preserve the same closed classes. There is no sufficiently distinct remainder to repair.
residual_risks: Eggarter full text was unavailable; that limitation does not alter the demonstrated direct coverage by earlier complete-split results.
No time-to-absorption estimate is in the frozen claim.

value.rationale: The contrast between exponentially many weak minima and two absorbing states is meaningful, but is already present when the exact complete-split census and attraction results are combined at a=2. Fixing the sign error in the proof would not change that conclusion.
